findings.title: TASK-039E accepted proposals are not materialized canonical Rule v1 documents
findings.evidence: The proposal DSL family is named canonical_delayed_response_rule_v1_candidate, but project proposal documents force canonical_rule_materialized=false and both authority flags false. The prepared validity result repeats those false flags. No TASK-039E construction path invokes parse_delayed_response_rule or materialize_accepted_rule.
findings.impact: Calling 42/42 or 39/42 'canonical rules accepted/authorized' would overstate the artifact lifecycle. Correct wording is relation-level prepared-validity admissible proposals / accepted_proposal outcomes.
findings.recommended_wording: The frozen construction arms produced evidence-bound proposal candidates that passed the TASK-039E deterministic prepared-validity adapter; this does not itself materialize canonical Rule v1 or grant runtime authority.

findings.title: Construction candidate semantics are broader than canonical Rule v1 MVP materialization
findings.evidence: Provider core permits step_up/step_down and target increase/decrease. Canonical DelayedResponseRuleV1 MVP parser requires expected effect direction increase and trigger state_changes_to. Therefore the candidate label must not be read as a proven one-to-one canonical materialization contract.
findings.impact: A direct proposal-to-canonical-rule bridge is not established by this construction audit; later utility/runtime projections must remain separately named and bound.

findings.title: Generic provider schema intentionally cannot prevent relation substitution alone
findings.evidence: source, target, and relation_identity are generic nonempty strings to avoid answer leakage. Exact identities, directions, horizon, and reference hashes are enforced only after parsing by prepared deterministic validity.
findings.impact: Documentation must attribute these guarantees to the verifier/binding layer, not the provider JSON schema or parser.

findings.title: Canonical schema breadth exceeds the currently supported MVP parser
findings.evidence: The JSON schema enumerates multiple triggers, relations, effects, windows, and output types, while _validate_mvp accepts a much smaller subset.
findings.impact: UI/reporting should document actual parser-supported semantics rather than reproduce schema enums as implemented capability.

supported: The construction proposal format is closed, typed, reference-bound, and non-executable.

Prepared deterministic validity rejects unsupported variables, relation changes, direction/horizon changes, unapproved numeric references/literals, free-form runtime logic, prohibited data references, stale hashes, and authority preclaims.
Runtime authorization is a separate explicit authority layer.
not_supported: An accepted TASK-039E proposal is already a canonical Rule v1.
Prepared-validity admissibility is equivalent to canonical VerifierV1 acceptance.
The broad schema enum set is fully implemented by the current MVP parser.
